page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Marginal note in the right margin, running across the paragraph beginning "Cæterum de iis". Running head centred above the text, page number at top right. Catchword at the lower right, signature at the lower left.

main_text.p: §.[?] Liber historiarum, ab Esaia scriptus: Beda, T.4. in Esdram,lib.2.cap.9.

Cæterùm,etsi ij libri ἀπόκρυφοι[?] desideren-tur: tamen nihil decedit de doctrina ad salu-tem nostram necessaria. Nam diuina proui-dentia tantum seruatum est librorum,quan-tum satis erat ad cognoscendum Deum, e-jus voluntatem, Christum, eoque viam sa-lutis.
Atque hæc de illis, quibus scriptura vete-ris Testamenti, de qua proprie loquitur Apostolus 2. Tim.3.satis.
Cæterum de iis, quibus scriptura NouiDe noui Testamen-ti scripto-ribus. Testamenti inspirata: & à quibus in literas redacta fuit, facilior & certior est responsio.
Extra controuersiam est, Euangelistas omnes sua scripsisse Euangelia, idque affla-tos Spiritu sancto. De actis Lucas ipse te-statur.

De Epistolis etiam Paulo ascriptis, nemo dubitat, quin à Paulo fuerint conscriptæ: si unam excipias ad Hebraeos. Sed nihil etiam est firmæ rationis, firmive testimonij, cur non sentiendum sit, fuisse & hanc à Paulo exaratam: cùm & Clemens Alexandrinus, & alij nonnulli antiqui Patres affirment.

De Epistolis Canonicis antea à nobis di-ctum fuit, quid sentiam: itidem de Apocaly-psi. Ego non dubito,omnes hosce libros ab illis fuisse scriptos, quibus etiam ascribun-tur, & quidem omnes Græca lingua. Nam quòd de Euangelio Matthaei & de Epistola ad

page.notes: The marginal note "De noui Testamenti scriptoribus" runs over four lines of the paragraph beginning "Cæterum de iis"; it is set in italic and is placed where it starts. The section sign at the start of the first line is doubtful [?]. The Greek word "ἀπόκρυφοι" is doubtful [?]; the first letters are hard to make out. The citation "2. Tim.3.satis." is read as printed, the numeral "2" is slightly uncertain. The signature "L j" is read as "L" and a j-like mark. The catchword "Hebraeos" is set at the lower right in italic. Long s has been converted to s throughout.
